Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the last session! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Tom Latham and Will Young are the two openers for New Zealand. Matthew Potts to start proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

That joy was short-lived for England as the introduction of spin from New Zealand completely changed the course of the game. Mitchell Santner removed Ollie Pope in the first over of his spell. He then got rid of the English skipper in his next over and added one more to his tally as well. Matt Henry finished the job with his fourth wicket, and the hosts, unlike England did not allow the opponent's tail to wag around for long. New Zealand have a first-inning lead of 204 runs and had the chance to enforce the follow-on. However, they will come out to bat and will be eyeing to set up a massive target with a lot of time left in the game. Join us around 3 am GMT to catch all the exciting action in the final session.

The English openers got off to a flier, getting the boundaries at will and putting the pressure back on the bowlers. However, a double-wicket over from Matt Henry halted their momentum and turned the game. Joe Root and Jacob Bethell steadied the ship for a bit, but then came that fantastic spell from William O'Rourke as he removed both in the same over and then added another to his tally as well. However, then-skipper Ben Stokes stiched up a 52-run stand along with Ollie Pope to get them back on track.

The umpires call for TEA with that last wicket of England! A terrific bowling performance from New Zealand and they are in a commanding position in the Test now. They completely dominated this session with William O'Rourke bowling a fantastic spell and getting three crucial wickets. England did show some resilience, but that was ended by the man of the moment, Mitchell Santner as he picked up three wickets in the space of 3 overs to get a firm grip on this game.

OUT! IN THE AIR....GONE! Matt Henry wraps things up here with his fourth wicket! He goes full and on middle, Matthew Potts backs away to loft it away but only manages to get a top edge. The ball goes high in the air and behind point where Glenn Phillips runs backward, settles under it and takes a good catch. England have been bowled out for just 143!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! The New Zealand players are in a huddle just outside the boundary ropes. Tom Latham is giving his team a last-minute pep talk, and now they spread out to take their respective field positions. Jacob Bethell and Joe Root to continue the batting for England. Matt Henry to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

The next session promises to be an exciting one. Can England continue to build on this foundation provided by the openers and post a big first innings total? Or will New Zealand with the hard new ball, come out blazing and ramble through this English lineup? Join us after Lunch at 12.40 am GMT to find out.

England would have hoped to pick up the last wicket early in the session, but they had to toil hard for that. Ben Stokes went to restrict the runs rather than going for the wicket which cost them a few crucial runs as they finally got the breakthrough after the drinks break. After, that both the openers came out all guns blazing with Zak Crawley hitting Tim Southee for four boundaries in the second over. However, Matt Henry turned things around by getting rid of Crawley for the fifth time and also picking up Ben Duckett as well. Joe Root and Jacob Bethell saw till the end of the session with England getting past 50.

SESSION SUMMARY - 86 runs and 3 wickets in 25.1 overs! New Zealand will be the happier side in this session! Earlier, it was Mitchell Santner with some good help from William O'Rourke, added some crucial runs for the last wicket. Then, that good work was followed up by the bowlers, especially Matt Henry who sent both the openers back in the same over. England though scored at a good rate despite the wickets and with conditions getting better for batting, they will be looking to chip into the lead in the next session.
Good length and just outside off, Joe Root gets in two minds but withdraws his bat at the last moment. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Would you believe it? Matt Henry gets Zak Crawley for the fifth time in this series, this time with a fantastic catch on his own bowling. He lands this on a hard length and on middle, angles in and then straightens a shy bit. Zak Crawley looks to work it away but closes the bat face early. It goes off the leading edge towards the bowler where Henry moves to his left, dives and grabs the ball just inches above the ground. Crawley is not sure about that and the umpires want to make sure as well. The replay shows that the fingers are underneath the ball and Crawley has to walk back after hitting a few lusty blows. England rocked early again!
